intro.title: From interface to infrastructure.
intro.body: I’m a full-stack developer who likes seeing the whole picture. From crafting interfaces to building backend systems and mobile apps, I enjoy turning complex problems into software that works, makes sense, and stands the test of time.

principle1.title: Break down complexity
principle1.description: I prefer to understand the underlying logic before jumping into implementation. Complex features become easier to reason about when their responsibilities and rules are clearly separated.
principle1.example: At SIGSCAN, I worked on an alert engine involving business rules and multiple system components. I approached the feature by breaking the logic into smaller, reusable parts rather than treating it as one large block of code.

principle2.title: Improve what exists
principle2.description: Not every problem needs a new feature or another layer of abstraction. Sometimes the best solution is to simplify what's already there and make future changes less painful.
principle2.example: In the Angular frontend, I refactored existing code and simplified repeated UI patterns, making the codebase easier to understand and work with.

principle3.title: Account for the real world
principle3.description: Software doesn't exist in isolation. Devices, external libraries and existing systems all have their own constraints, and the implementation needs to account for them.
principle3.example: In the Android inventory app, I worked with Zebra RFID hardware and its SDK, integrating device-level functionality into the application rather than treating it as a purely software problem.

principle4.title: Think beyond the code
principle4.description: A feature needs to make sense to the person using it, not just work technically. I value clear interfaces and making sure the implementation reflects the actual requirements.
principle4.example: Working with Angular, I implemented interfaces from Figma designs, including responsive layouts, forms and navigation, while integrating them with application logic and access permissions.

beyond-code.title: Beyond the code
beyond-code.paragraph1: I'm curious about the world beyond the screen. With a background in international politics, I enjoy exploring different cultures, discovering places off the beaten path, and diving into history. I like understanding how things came to be — whether that's a piece of software, a historical site, or a society.
beyond-code.paragraph2: That curiosity is part of what I bring to development: a willingness to look beyond the obvious, ask questions, and understand the bigger picture.
